chunks: Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa narrated from al-Husayn ibn Sa'id, from al-Nadr ibn Suwayd, from Hisham ibn Salim, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:
I said to him, 'Are prayers offered for the drinker of wine, the fornicator, and the thief when they die?' He said, 'Yes.'

key_terms.يُصَلَّى عَلَيْهِمْ: Prayers are offered for them (funeral prayer)

ai.seo_question: Do we pray funeral prayers for sinners who die?
ai.summary: Imam al-Sadiq (AS) confirms that major sinners (fasiqun), including wine drinkers, fornicators, and thieves, remain eligible for funeral prayers, affirming the general rule that specific major sins do not automatically exclude one from communal ritual duties. This ruling reflects the Shia scholarly consensus that salat al-janazah is a communal obligation (fard kifaya) performed for the deceased regardless of their moral state, serving as a means of mercy and intercession rather than a declaration of their ultimate salvation. It underscores the distinction between the ritual act of prayer and the theological judgment of the individual's final standing with God.
